what_its_for: Diflorasone diacetate is a strong steroid cream or ointment used on your skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on your skin only. Do NOT put it in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. Wash your hands before and after applying. Clean and dry the affected skin area gently. Apply a thin layer of the cream or ointment and rub it in gently. Do not cover the treated area with bandages, plastic wrap, or tight clothing unless your doctor tells you to. Only apply it to the area your doctor told you to treat.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 1 to 3 times per day, or exactly as your doctor instructs. Use the smallest amount needed to control your symptoms. Do not use more than your doctor prescribed, and do not use it for longer than directed. This is a very strong steroid, so your doctor will likely want you to use it for only a short time.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double amount to make up for the missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply this medicine to your face, underarms, or groin area unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes or mouth. Do not use other steroid skin products on the same area unless your doctor approves. Avoid using skin products that may irritate your skin, such as harsh soaps, perfumes, or exfoliants, on the treated area. Do not wrap or bandage the treated skin tightly, as this can increase absorption of the medicine and raise the risk of side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical attention if you notice: skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising on the treated area; unusual weight gain, especially around your face or belly; extreme tiredness or weakness; vision changes; signs of skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or pain; signs of allergic reaction such as hives, rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat. Also call your doctor if your skin condition is not improving after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms such as reduced itching and redness within a few days of starting treatment. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks to see the full benefit. If your skin is not getting better after 2 weeks, let your doctor know.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children because their skin absorbs more of this medicine, which raises the risk of serious side effects. Use the lowest effective amount for the shortest time possible, and only under doctor supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. It should only be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding if the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Avoid applying to the chest area if breastfeeding. Elderly: Older adults may have thinner skin and may be more sensitive to side effects. Use with caution as directed by your doctor.
